title: Liquor Control director retirement and replacement search
summary: At a September 21 special meeting, the Liquor Control Commission voted unanimously for an open application process and for a temporary investigative group to hire a search firm and gather, screen and rank applicants. The director announced September 9 that he will retire December 31. The last search took about eight months, and November 23 is held for a possible interview-prep meeting.

upcomingEvent.what: possible special meeting to prepare for interviews

timeline.text: Director hiring is a standing item on the regular agenda and can be discussed at the October meeting.
November 23 was held for a possible special meeting to prepare for interviews.
The group will hire a search firm and work with it to gather, screen and rank applications.
The commission voted unanimously to create a temporary investigative group, a small team that works outside public meetings.
The commission voted unanimously for an open application process.
The director said the last search took about eight months.
The job requires five years of law enforcement experience, three of them in administrative work.
The deputy corporation counsel said the county rule calls for a hiring process open to any candidate.
The director of the Department of Liquor Control announced his retirement at the commission's last meeting.
The Liquor Control Commission held a special meeting.
A special meeting is set for September 21 at 1:30 p.m. to discuss how to find a new director.
The department director said he will retire, with December 31 as his last day.
